actual_class_and_dom_reachability: Owned select provides MatLegacyFormFieldControl using the owned select instance. The legacy-form-field public API reexports the actual current public MatFormFieldControl as MatLegacyFormFieldControl. Owned form-field queries that public control token, reads the owned base's controlType='mat-select', and adds classPrefix='mat-form-field-type-' plus that controlType. Its host disabled class binds to _control.disabled. This produces the exact ancestor/disabled predicates consumed by the existing historical cursor rule.

The owned form-field template places .mat-form-field-flex inside .mat-form-field-wrapper and binds its click to _control.onContainerClick($event). Prefix/infix/suffix are descendants of the flex region. Label-wrapper/label and outline pointer-events rules were reviewed; the cursor rule targets the clickable flex region, not subscript, underline or the outer host. The original patch title's entire form field wording does not authorize widening the historical cursor region to every host descendant.

Both actual minimum public peer form-field implementations query MatFormFieldControl, generate classPrefix='mat-mdc-form-field-type-' plus control.controlType, and bind mat-form-field-disabled to _control.disabled. Their templates contain .mat-mdc-text-field-wrapper, with the same control click delegate, enclosing the modern flex/infix/prefix/suffix region. Both actual minimum peer select styles contain the exact enabled-only modern-wrapper rule from the original patch.

The public current form-field can discover the legacy control token alias, and the owned controlType remains mat-select. Therefore a current form-field containing a legacy select can produce the modern ancestor class and can match the original peer cursor selector if the current-select component CSS is actually loaded. The patched selector is not restricted to a current-select host element. Merely inheriting or owning a select base does not prove this CSS path unreachable.

Conversely the peer modern-wrapper selector does not target the ordinary legacy form-field flex region, and the historical flex selector does not target the modern text-field wrapper. Both enabled paths and both disabled exclusions were checked against source-derived class predicates and template regions. These are source topology checks, not rendered CSS-cascade observations.
